text: {"score":2,"justification":"Numbers match the card, and the two cited claims are real high-complexity 99215 examples. But the interpretation and next steps are poorly grounded. The headline and leaning ('consistent with high acuity panel', 'low-complexity rates are near peers') are contradicted by the card: the provider's 99215 share is 3.81x expected (z 4.17), and the provider's rate exceeds the all-provider rate in every complexity band (e.g., 10.7% vs 2.2% at 0 conditions, 17.7% vs 7.4% at 3). The first next step says 'the documentation returned supports the level billed', yet zero records came back and documentation is empty, so this is false and conflicts with the summary's own statement. An investigator would be misled into closing the case. The summary also has no concrete step such as requesting records for the low-complexity 99215 claims, and it never cites those claims.","problems":["Headline claims low-complexity rates are near peers, but the card shows provider rates 2-5x the all-provider rates in most bands (0 conditions 10.7% vs 2.2%; 3 conditions 17.7% vs 7.4%; 5+ 51% vs 19.5%).","Rationale cherry-picks 1-2 condition bands (6.6-6.7% vs 3.4-5.3%) to claim near-peer rates; this misrepresents the table.","Next step says documentation returned supports the level billed, but 0 records returned and no documentation exists; contradicts the summary's own text.","'Do not pursue recovery' is unsupported given a 3.81x ratio to expected and z of 4.17; the leaning toward a high-acuity panel downplays the strong statistical signal.","No actionable step to request records for the cited or low-complexity 99215 claims (e.g., C0012483, C0012524, C0012538 with 0 conditions); low-complexity claims are not cited.","Cited examples are only high-complexity claims, which support the benign framing but not the excess; evidence selection is one-sided.","Fragmented wording ('Records not requested. Claims only.') conflicts with 'Records came back for 0 claims.'"]}
